title: Paul & Mike and Tata Starbucks Turn Coffee Into Diwali Chocolate
excerpt: The limited-edition collection pairs a Caramel Macchiato chocolate with Saffron Pista and Pista Katli, in a 12-piece box priced at Rs 990 at select Starbucks stores across India.
body:
• TATA Starbucks and Indian fine chocolate maker Paul & Mike have launched a limited-edition Diwali chocolate collection, now at select Starbucks stores across India.
  • The 12-piece handcrafted box (116g) costs Rs 990; the Chocolate Berry Crunch (100g) costs Rs 450.
  • Flavours pair Starbucks coffee notes with Indian festive staples: Caramel Macchiato, Saffron Pista and Pista Katli, plus Hazelnut Praline and Cashew Cremino.
  • For diaspora readers, it is a sendable, store-bought Diwali gift in India — no courier needed if family can pick it up locally.

Diwali gifting in India has a new entry this year, and it comes in a Starbucks box. TATA Starbucks has partnered with homegrown fine chocolate brand Paul & Mike on a limited-edition collection that translates coffee flavours into chocolate and pairs them with Indian festive staples, HospiBuz reports. The collection is on sale for a limited period at select TATA Starbucks stores across India.

What is in the box

The centrepiece is a box of 12 handcrafted chocolates (116g) priced at Rs 990. The assortment moves between coffee-inspired pieces and festive ones: a Caramel Macchiato chocolate sits alongside Saffron Pista and Pista Katli, with Hazelnut Praline and Cashew Cremino rounding out the range. Alongside it, the Chocolate Berry Crunch (100g, Rs 450) is a dark chocolate rocher built with toasted quinoa, tart cranberries and crunchy pumpkin seeds, sold in joint Paul & Mike and Starbucks festive packaging, according to BW Retail World.

"People are looking for gifts that feel thoughtful, distinctive and personal."

— Mitali Maheshwari, Head of Product and Marketing, TATA Starbucks

Maheshwari said the way Diwali is celebrated keeps evolving while the sentiment behind it — bringing people together and showing them they matter — stays the same. Vikas Temani, founder of Paul & Mike, said chocolatiers from both teams worked together on the assortment and described the partnership as a meeting of craftsmanship and innovation aimed at festive gifting in India.

Why brands chase the Diwali gift box

Festive gifting is one of the most contested shelves in Indian retail, and coffee chains have been pushing beyond beverages into food and merchandise that travel well as gifts. A chocolate box solves a practical problem for the giver: it is priced below the Rs 1,000 line that anchors much corporate and family gifting, it keeps without refrigeration worries that mithai carries, and it reads as contemporary while still using the flavours — saffron, pistachio, katli — that signal Diwali. For Paul & Mike, a Kerala-born bean-to-bar maker, shelf space inside Starbucks stores across India is distribution that a young chocolate brand cannot build on its own.

For readers abroad

The diaspora angle is practical. If you are sending Diwali wishes to family in India this year, the collection can be bought in-store by the recipient or ordered for them locally at select TATA Starbucks outlets, at Rs 990 for the gift box and Rs 450 for the Berry Crunch — no international shipping, no melted chocolate in transit. Availability is limited to the festive period, so it is a buy-it-now item rather than one to bookmark for later in the season.
